jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Partner Integrations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Recognized on the 2025 Forbes Cloud 100 list, ClickHouse is one of the most innovative and fast-growing private cloud companies. With more than 4,000 customers and $250M ARR, ClickHouse leads the market in real-time analytics, data warehousing, observability, and AI workloads.

The company's sustained, accelerating momentum was recently validated by a $400M Series D financing round. Over the past three months, customers including Capital One, Lovable, Decagon, Polymarket, and Airwallex have adopted the platform or expanded existing deployments. These customers join an established base of AI innovators and global brands such as Meta, Cursor, Sony, and Tesla.

We're on a mission to transform how companies use data. Come be a part of our journey!

We're hiring a Product Manager to own partner integrations at ClickHouse. This role owns how ClickHouse shows up inside the platforms our customers already use: embedded, native experiences across the hyperscalers and developer platforms, and deeper technical integrations with strategic partners like dbt, Fivetran, Hex, and Sigma. There is a growing surface of partner work already in motion, and this role shapes where we invest in co-innovation opportunities.

This is one of the most cross-functional roles at ClickHouse. You'll work across multiple engineering teams, our partnerships and solutions teams, and the partners themselves to deliver meaningful co-innovation and integrations with complementary technologies. You'll own the technical side of our House Mates partner program and be the person who navigates the multi-org reality of getting an integration certified, listed, and live. This is a hands-on role: you'll write the specs, run the partner calls, drive certification processes, and coordinate across teams to get things over the line.

You Will

  • Own the product strategy, roadmap, and execution for ClickHouse's Cloud integrations with strategic partners

  • Seek out complementary innovation opportunities with partners. Define what a "better together" integration looks like with each strategic partner, and drive it from joint roadmap through launch.

  • Navigate the trade-offs of embedded integrations: billing and metering, identity and auth, security and data residency, and coordination across ClickHouse and partner teams.

  • Project-manage complex, multi-org launches: marketplace listings, certification processes, partner co-marketing, and GA timelines across multiple organizations.

  • Own the technical standards and certification criteria for integrations submitted through the House Mates partner program.

  • Measure and communicate co-innovation business impact, adoption and product strategy to executive leadership.

  • Represent ClickHouse externally at partner events and in joint content.

You Bring

  • Experience shipping integrations into third-party platforms before: hyperscaler marketplaces, embedded or native integrations, ISV partnerships, or OEM/white-label work.

  • An understanding of the trade-offs that make or break a partner integration, billing, auth, security, cross-team dependencies, and have made those decisions in the past.

  • A strong project management lens and are comfortable owning a launch that depends on five teams across two companies.

  • Patience and resilience with partners who are unresponsive or have their own competing priorities, and you find creative ways to keep things moving anyway.

  • Technical ability to understand an integration end to end, from provisioning and auth to billing and data flow, and to hold a credible conversation with engineers about APIs, architecture, and technical trade-offs.

  • Energy and excitement for external-facing work: partner calls, customer conversations, and representing the product publicly.

  • Hands-on and high ownership ability. You write the specs, run the partner calls, and stay close to the details.

  • Comfort in ambiguity and fast-moving environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience building partner integrations with hyperscalers and modern technology companies.

  • Experience running or supporting a technology partner program.

  • Background at a database or data infrastructure company; familiarity with ClickHouse or peers like Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks.

  • Experience working in remote, multi-timezone environments.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

Equal Opportunity & Privacy

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer - ClickPipes Platform
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team

The ClickPipes team builds the services that power data ingestion into ClickHouse Cloud. As a primary entry point for customers’ data, ClickPipes is critical to product adoption and the company’s growth. We work at petabyte scale, solving challenges in distributed systems, fault tolerance, and high-throughput ingestion. You’ll help make these pipelines performant, reliable, and easy to operate, with ownership of technical decisions and the platform as a whole.

You can find some of the team’s recent work highlighted in our blog:

  • GCP Pub/Sub connector for ClickPipes is now in Private Preview

  • Terraform & OpenAPI for ClickPipes is now Generally Available

  • Unordered mode for GCS ClickPipes is now available

We’re looking for backend engineers with experience in data-intensive systems who enjoy working across technologies. You’ll collaborate with engineering and product partners and drive projects from design through production.

What will you do?

  • Build and evolve integrations with streaming platforms and object storage, including Kafka, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, S3, GCS, and Azure Blob Storage.

  • Continuously improve our systems based on operational metrics, customer feedback, and evolving business requirements.

  • Drive technical discussions and contribute to architectural decisions that impact our platform's scalability and resilience.

  • Participate in on-call rotations to ensure system reliability and respond to production incidents.

About you:

  • 5+ years of software development experience building and operating distributed systems.

  • Strong knowledge of Go and its ecosystem.

  • Experience designing systems for scalability and fault tolerance, with an understanding of concurrency, consistency, and failure recovery.

  • Understanding of cloud-native architecture and practical experience with at least one major cloud provider.

  • Experience diagnosing and resolving production issues in distributed systems.

  • Ability to communicate technical ideas clearly and collaborate across engineering and product teams.

  • Experience with data ingestion pipelines, streaming platforms, or object storage is a plus.

Perks

jobs.title: Manager, Commercial Operations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Manager, Commercial Operations

We are looking for a Manager of Commercial Operations to build and run the transactional engine of the commercial function inside Revenue Operations. ClickHouse runs on a usage-based pricing model, and every deal – direct, marketplace, or partner – has to land correctly in the system: quoted against the right rules, ordered against the right contract structure, and booked cleanly enough that Accounting can bill and recognize it without rework. As we scale the cloud business and widen the product line, that path has to carry more volume, more products, and more deal structures without adding people to the middle of it. This role designs the systems, automation, and controls that make that possible.

Reporting to the Director, Commercial Strategy & Operations, you will own the quote-to-order path and order management, along with the build behind it: the CPQ and quoting system requirements, the automation, the validation and controls, and marketplace transaction operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure. The goal is a commercial path where the standard deal is self-service for the field, quality is enforced by the system rather than by who touched the deal, and human review is reserved for the cases that genuinely need judgment. You will be measured by how fast and how cleanly a deal moves, how little intervention it requires, and how good the experience is for the rep. You will partner daily with Sales, Accounting, Finance, Legal, and Revenue Engineering.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • Own order management and automate it. Run the intake, review, and processing of quotes, order forms, and bookings to defined SLAs through quarter-end peaks, and continuously engineer the manual steps out of that path.

  • Design the quote-to-order flow. Instrument the process, find where it slows or breaks, and redesign it. You own the architecture of the flow, the exception routing, and the automation that makes the standard case hands-off.

  • Own the quoting and order management system build. Write the requirements, design the quoting, validation, and approval logic, drive the roadmap with Revenue Engineering, run UAT, and validate every change in production before the field sees it.

  • Own the handoff into billing and revenue. Partner with Accounting so that what leaves your process arrives structured, complete, and reconcilable – and build the controls upstream that keep downstream rework from happening at all.

  • Build quality in as controls. Validation rules, guided quoting, required-field logic, and automated reconciliation that make an incorrect order hard to submit in the first place.

  • Own the field experience of transacting. Treat the rep as the customer: fewer steps, fewer handoffs, shorter quote cycle time, and a standard path that is obvious and self-service. Measure whether it is getting easier.

  • Build and run marketplace transaction operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure. Private offers, CSP transactions, co-sell mechanics, and the tooling and automated reconciliation that keep marketplace bookings tied out across the marketplace, Salesforce, and billing.

  • Operationalize commercial review. Encode approval rules and guardrails in the system so routine deals route themselves, and escalate the structures that break the system rather than quietly processing them.

  • Build the transaction path for new products and acquisitions. Stand up order management, quoting, and the marketplace path for new offerings and newly acquired products, test the flow through to booking before go-live, and be ready to transact on day one.

  • Own the integrity of the commercial record. Products, SKUs, pricing, contract terms, and booking attributes in Salesforce, with the controls and monitoring that keep them clean – the forecast and revenue reporting downstream depend on it.

  • Instrument and report on the system you own. Cycle time, touch count, SLA attainment, exception and discount volumes, error and rework rates. Use the data to decide what gets built next.

WHAT YOU BRING ALONG

  • 6+ years in commercial operations, deal desk, order management, sales operations, or revenue operations, including time owning a high-volume transactional process.

  • A track record of building, not just running. You have replaced a manual process with a designed one and can point to the automation, the controls, and the measured result.

  • Hands-on depth in Salesforce and Salesforce CPQ. You write requirements, design quoting and approval logic, configure and test it yourself, and can tell a configuration problem from a process problem.

  • Technical range beyond the admin console: flows and validation logic, API-based and marketplace integrations, and scripting or SQL to reconcile and investigate data at volume. You can partner with Revenue Engineering as a peer on design.

  • Experience with usage-based or consumption-based contracts: metering, commits, overages, contract structure, and the downstream billing and revenue recognition implications.

  • Experience operating across a shared quote-to-cash process. You know where order management ends and Accounting begins, and you design the handoff so neither side is cleaning up after the other.

  • Marketplace operations experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure – private offers, CSP transactions, and reconciliation – strongly preferred.

  • Process-engineering instincts. You instrument before you optimize, design for the standard case and route the exception, and measure by throughput and error rate rather than activity.

  • A bias toward field experience. You have made a transactional process materially faster or simpler for a sales team and can describe how you knew it worked.

  • Comfort partnering with Accounting, Finance, and Legal on order form and contract mechanics.

  • Sound judgment under deal pressure. You can hold the line on a structure that breaks the system, and advocate for the field when the exception is justified.

  • Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain a commercial rule to a rep in one paragraph and brief leadership on what's at risk at quarter-end.

  • Experience managing or mentoring analysts a plus; this role is expected to grow a team as volume scales.

  • Bachelor's degree, quantitative or technical field preferred.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

 - Hands-on depth in Salesforce and Salesforce CPQ. You write requirements, design quoting and approval logic, configure and test it yourself, and can tell a configuration problem from a process problem.

jobs.title: Regional Field Marketing, India
jobs.descriptionHtml:
ClickHouse is hiring for our Regional Field Marketing, India role to lead our regional field marketing strategy in India. This is a foundational role responsible for building awareness, generating pipeline, and accelerating revenue in the region.

In this role, your mission will be to define and scale the India regional field marketing engine. You will own the regional field marketing strategy, partner closely with India sales leadership, and adapt global campaigns to the needs of the India market. You will be measured on enterprise pipeline and self-service revenue (MRR), working across both our self-serve product-led motion and our sales-led enterprise motion.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Own the India regional field marketing strategy, annual plan, and budget, aligning field programs to regional pipeline and revenue targets with sales leadership.

  • Act as the marketing counterpart to India sales leadership, joining regional forecasting, QBRs, and account planning so marketing investment maps to sales priorities.

  • Partner with demand generation and growth to build programs for strategic verticals and AI-native sales teams, and to convert self-serve usage into commercial pipeline and expansion revenue.

  • Build an integrated regional program mix spanning first-party hosted events, third-party conferences, virtual events, ABM plays, digital advertising, and partner marketing.

  • Adapt global campaigns, messaging, and content for the India market.

  • Establish scalable processes for campaign planning, lead management, and follow-up with marketing operations and global demand generation, so every program has a clear path from engagement to pipeline. Report on pipeline generated and influenced revenue.

  • Identify emerging opportunities across India, make the case for new investment in geographies, verticals, or channels, and represent the region in global planning cycles.

What You Bring Along

  • 10+ years of experience in field, regional, or integrated marketing within the database, data analytics, infrastructure, or developer tooling space

  • Deep experience marketing in India

  • Demonstrated success owning a pipeline number and driving measurable revenue impact through regional marketing programs

  • Proven ability to partner with sales leadership at the VP level

  • Experience working in a remote-first, globally distributed organization, collaborating across time zones

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and energized by building in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive-Melbourne
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The Role

You’ll own a net-new enterprise territory in Melbourne. Most of your number comes from accounts that don’t buy from us yet.

New business usually starts with a team already running ClickHouse — open source, or a Cloud account someone expensed — until a bill or a security review pushes the conversation up to the platform team and the budget owner. Common triggers: an Elasticsearch or Splunk bill that’s hard to defend, a warehouse that can’t serve a customer-facing feature fast enough, an AI product querying tens of billions of rows.

You’ll carry a small set of existing accounts alongside the hunt, where growth comes from new teams inside an account that already buys from us. One team lands a workload, it works, and four other teams have a similar problem. But the bulk of this role is finding and opening accounts that aren’t on our map yet.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Own the full sales cycle for new accounts in your territory — first conversation through security review, procurement, and close, on Cloud commitments and multi-year committed spend.

  • Build your own pipeline. Self-sourced outbound is the primary input to this territory, not a supplement to inbound.

  • Find and convert existing ClickHouse usage in new accounts. Unmanaged open-source deployments and self-serve Cloud accounts are the highest-yield source of new pipeline in this segment.

  • Multi-thread across the data platform team, the budget owner, security, and the executive sponsor rather than relying on a single champion.

  • Work with your Solutions Architect through the technical evaluation. They own the technical win, you own the commercial strategy and the close.

  • Run the procurement path: security questionnaires, legal redlines, vendor onboarding, and BYOC or private-deployment requirements, including Australian data residency where it’s required.

  • Give your champion the internal business case — TCO comparison against the incumbent, migration plan, and risk mitigation.

  • Grow the accounts you land by mapping the remaining teams and use cases and building an expansion plan against them.

  • Watch consumption trends across your accounts and engage early when usage flattens or spikes. Both are signals.

  • Keep Salesforce accurate and submit a forecast leadership can plan against.

  • Participate in the developer community in your territory: meetups, conferences, and events across Melbourne.

What You Bring

  • 6+ years selling technical infrastructure to enterprise buyers — databases, data platforms, cloud infrastructure, observability, or developer tooling.

  • A track record of self-sourced pipeline. You can explain your weekly prospecting approach and what actually works for you.

  • Experience selling into Melbourne and Victorian enterprise accounts, and familiarity with how procurement and security review run here.

  • A track record closing complex deals that went through security review, legal, and procurement.

  • Enough technical fluency to hold an architecture conversation. You don’t need to write SQL, but you should be able to explain why a company moves a workload off Elasticsearch.

  • Experience with consumption-based or usage-metered commercial models, where revenue moves with usage between contract events.

  • Experience selling into developer-led, bottom-up adoption as well as top-down.

  • Ability to orchestrate people who don’t report to you — Solutions Architects, executive sponsors, partners, product managers.

  • Comfort building a territory from scratch rather than inheriting mature coverage.

  • Accurate forecasting, including when the number is bad.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer - RBAC & Authorization
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team The Access Control team owns authorization across ClickHouse Cloud. We design and enforce the roles and permissions model, organization hierarchies, API key management, and security boundaries that every product surface and tenant depends on. Having recently shipped custom roles and fine-grained access, we are now evolving our architecture to support our largest enterprise customer structures.

What You Will Do

  • Architect and build the next generation of our authorization model: multi-level organization hierarchies, workspace isolation, and resource-scoped roles.

  • Implement and enforce consistent authorization checks across all public and internal APIs.

  • Build tooling and migration pipelines to evolve live authorization models without downtime or customer disruption.

  • Partner cross-functionally with Product, Design, and Customer Identity teams to deliver seamless permission management UIs.

What We Are Looking For

  • Experience: 6+ years building security platforms, access control engines, or core backend services at scale.

  • Domain Expertise: Deep knowledge of RBAC/ABAC policy models, fine-grained permission enforcement, multi-tenancy isolation, API keys, and SAML/SSO.

  • Core Stack: Excellent TypeScript/Node.js fundamentals and strong schema design skills in PostgreSQL or relational stores.

  • Migration Discipline: Proven track record of executing live customer data migrations and building high-correctness systems where failure is not an option.

Ideal Backgrounds: Enterprise identity platforms, IAM security tools, zero-trust cloud infrastructure, or core authorization teams at major B2B SaaS companies.

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer - SysAdmin & Internal Ops Platform
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team The SysAdmin team owns ClickHouse Cloud's internal operations ecosystem: the web application, backend admin APIs, and CLI tooling used by SRE, Support, Billing, Sales Ops, and Engineering to inspect and operate on customer fleets. Our mission is to make high-stakes operational actions safe, audited, and frictionless.

What You Will Do

  • Architect and scale the internal SysAdmin console, admin APIs, and Go-based CLI plugins used across the company.

  • Enforce safety mechanisms on high-impact actions: fine-grained permissions, staff SSO enforcement, scoped service tokens, guardrails, and immutable audit logging.

  • Build unified integrations across third-party platforms (Salesforce, Pylon, billing platforms, feature flags) to surface holistic customer state in one pane.

  • Partner directly with internal stakeholders (Support, SREs, Sales Ops) to eliminate operational toil and streamline crisis response workflows.

What We Are Looking For

  • Experience: 6+ years in full-stack software engineering, specifically building back-office tooling, admin consoles, or internal developer platforms.

  • Core Stack: Strong TypeScript/Node.js and React for dense, data-heavy UIs. Experience or willingness to write Go for CLI tooling is a major plus.

jobs.title: Regional VP, Southwest
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The Role

We're hiring our first Regional Vice President for the Southwest. The territory runs from the Rockies (Colorado and Utah) through Arizona and the desert Southwest to Southern California. It covers some of the fastest-growing tech corridors in the country, plus a dense base of digital-native, media, gaming, and AI companies that already run on real-time data. You'll report to Mike Hayes and build the region from the first hire: set the strategy, recruit the team, and turn a widely spread, high-potential territory into one of the strongest regions in the Americas. This is a builder's seat with a clear path to grow with the business.

What You'll Do

  • Design a multi-hub region. Build a coverage model across hubs that are very different from one another, including Los Angeles, Orange County, San Diego, Denver/Boulder, Salt Lake City/Lehi, and Phoenix. Decide where to place reps first and how to sequence growth.

  • Hire the founding team. Recruit Enterprise AEs who can sell to engineering buyers as peers: technical, commercially hungry, and able to work on their own across a large geography.

  • Own the number and the forecast. Carry the regional quota, run a weekly operating rhythm, and deliver a forecast your leadership can rely on, backed by MEDDPICC-style deal qualification.

  • Win where real-time data is the product. Land and expand with digital-native and AI-native companies, media and entertainment, gaming, adtech, consumer internet, and fintech, where performance and cost at scale decide the deal.

  • Turn adoption into enterprise agreements. Work with our product-led growth motion to find ClickHouse Cloud and open-source users ready for a committed relationship, then expand across teams and use cases (analytics, observability, and AI workloads).

  • Lead from inside the deal. Coach reps through technical evaluations, POCs, procurement, and executive negotiations. Join the calls that matter.

  • Orchestrate the extended team. Partner closely with Solutions Architects, Marketing, Partners/Alliances, and cloud marketplace teams to build pipeline and run cohesive account strategies.

  • Build ClickHouse's brand across the region. Show up in the local developer, data, and startup communities, from Denver and Salt Lake to LA and San Diego, through events, meetups, and executive programs.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years of enterprise software sales in data infrastructure, databases, analytics, observability, or cloud, with a strong record as a quota-carrying seller.

  • 5+ years leading enterprise sales teams as a first- or second-line leader, with attainment you can back up with specifics.

  • Experience building or rebuilding a region from an early stage, ideally one spread across several metros, where you set coverage, hired the first reps, and grew the business.

  • A strong network across the Rockies, the Southwest, and/or Southern California, both for hiring standout AEs and for reaching enterprise buyers.

  • Rigorous pipeline management, deal qualification (MEDDPICC or similar), and forecast accuracy.

  • Technical credibility with engineering-led buyers. You understand the modern data stack and can hold your own in architecture conversations.

  • Experience with consumption-based pricing, open-source, or product-led growth models.

  • The ClickHouse DNA: integrity, hunger, and accountability. You're curious, serious about the craft, and want to build rather than inherit.

Nice to Have

  • Experience selling to digital-native, AI-native, media/entertainment, or gaming companies.

  • A background in real-time analytics, OLAP and columnar databases, observability, or AI/LLM infrastructure.

  • Experience as an early leader at a high-growth data or infrastructure company through a period of fast scaling.

  • Co-selling with AWS, GCP, or Azure, and transacting through cloud marketplaces.

  • Experience leading a distributed team across several states and time zones.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

jobs.title: Regional VP, Southeast
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The Role

We're hiring our first Regional Vice President for the Southeast. You'll be the founding sales leader for the region. You'll hire and lead a team of Enterprise AEs, set the operating standard, and turn a strong base of developer adoption and ClickHouse Cloud sign-ups into a durable enterprise business. If you've been an early leader in a region before and want to do it again with a technically differentiated product, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

  • Build the region from the ground up. Own the Southeast territory plan, including which accounts, verticals, and metros to prioritize first, and where to place each new rep.

  • Recruit and close top-tier AEs. Use your regional network to hire a team of Enterprise AEs and keep growing it. Hire for technical curiosity, a proven record against a number, and high integrity.

  • Own the number. Carry the regional quota and forecast it accurately every week, month, and quarter. Run rigorous pipeline and deal reviews using a MEDDPICC-style qualification standard.

  • Land and expand enterprise accounts. Convert existing ClickHouse Cloud and open-source usage into committed enterprise agreements, then grow them as new use cases emerge. The Southeast's enterprise base spans financial services, payments, healthcare, logistics, retail, and media.

  • Get into deals. Join executive meetings, pressure-test deal strategy, and help reps through complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles involving technical buyers, procurement, and security review.

  • Run a tight team with Solutions Architects. Work hand in hand with SAs and SEs so every opportunity is technically sound and every customer is set up to grow.

  • Work the full GTM machine. Partner with Marketing, Partners/Alliances (including cloud marketplaces), and our product-led growth motion to build pipeline and pick up self-serve accounts ready for a sales-assisted conversation.

  • Be ClickHouse's face in the Southeast. Build our presence with customers, partners, and the local data and developer community through executive events, meetups, and field programs.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years of enterprise software sales in data infrastructure, databases, analytics, observability, or cloud, including a strong record as a quota-carrying seller.

  • 5+ years leading enterprise sales teams as a first- or second-line leader, with consistent attainment you can walk us through number by number.

  • A record of building a region or team from an early stage: hiring the first reps, defining territories, and growing a new geography into a predictable business.

  • A deep Southeast network of enterprise AEs, customers, and partners, and a reputation that makes strong sellers want to work for you.

  • Forecasting and qualification discipline (MEDDPICC or similar). You know the difference between a commit and a hope, and your leadership can trust your call.

  • Technical fluency. You can talk architecture with data engineers and CTOs, and you can tell when a deal is stalling for technical reasons and when it's commercial.

  • Experience with consumption-based or usage-based pricing models, and an understanding that in a consumption business the signed deal is where the revenue starts.

  • The ClickHouse DNA: integrity, hunger, and accountability. You're curious, serious about the craft, and happy to roll up your sleeves.

Nice to Have

  • Experience as an early sales leader or early seller in the Southeast at a high-growth data or infrastructure company.

  • Background selling open-source or developer-led products alongside a product-led growth funnel.

  • Familiarity with real-time analytics, OLAP and columnar databases, observability, or AI/LLM workloads.

  • Established relationships with data and technology leaders at major Southeast enterprises.

  • Experience co-selling with AWS, GCP, or Azure and transacting through cloud marketplaces.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

jobs.title: Technical Account Manager Architect - EMEA (Israel)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
ClickHouse is the open-source, real-time analytical database behind a lot of today's AI. More than 4,000 companies build on ClickHouse, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Tesla and Meta.

As a TAM Architect, you're the named technical lead for a small group of our largest customers. You carry the context of how they run ClickHouse, guide them from their first design decisions through production and growth, and make sure the rest of ClickHouse shows up for them when it matters. Your job is to keep them healthy, help them get more out of ClickHouse, and spot the next use case.

You'll work inside our Support organisation and own escalations for your accounts, working closely with our support engineers. The role is based in Israel, close to some of our biggest customers in EMEA.

Large enterprises are moving onto ClickHouse fast, and we're building out how we look after them. People joining now have a real say in how this role works.

What you'll do

  • Run a regular cadence with 4 to 8 strategic accounts (weekly, fortnightly or monthly, depending on the project), plus quarterly health checks and business reviews, on site where it helps

  • Lead onboarding, where the decisions that are hardest to reverse get made: schema and data modelling, table engines, ingestion, migration and query design

  • Once customers are live, keep performance and cost on track as they grow, and help them onto new use cases

  • Work closely with Support: own escalations for your accounts, with regular case reviews and a direct line into L3 engineering

  • Work with the right people for each piece of work: partner with Solutions Architects on new use cases and proof of concepts, and bring in Consulting Engineers for hands-on projects

  • Write it down: documented setup and configuration, knowledge base articles and reference architectures that help other customers too

What you'll bring

  • 5+ years in a hands-on, customer-facing technical role after the sale, whether your title was TAM, solutions architect, professional services, senior support or something else

  • Specialist depth in data modelling, query performance and integration on distributed or analytical databases

  • Hands-on SQL. You regularly write complex queries from scratch, and tune and debug them yourself

  • Experience owning a small book of high-touch enterprise accounts, where you know each customer's architecture in depth

  • Hands-on cloud experience (AWS, GCP and/or Azure)

  • You've run distributed systems, such as distributed databases, in production

  • You explain technical trade-offs clearly, to engineers and to executives

  • Fluent English and Hebrew

Nice to have

  • Experience with ClickHouse, or with other analytical databases such as Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift or Druid

  • Involvement in open source, as a user, contributor or community member

  • A working knowledge of Kubernetes

Good to know

  • You'll be based in Israel. Travel to customer sites is part of the job, up to 35% of your time, within Israel and throughout EMEA

  • You'll join our EMEA Support Services team, where Support Engineers, Consulting Engineers and TAM Architects work as one team

  • You'll be part of the on-call rota, about one week a quarter, with time off in lieu if you're paged at a weekend

How we hire

  • A 30-minute call with our recruiter

  • A conversation with the hiring manager

  • A take-home exercise, designed to take four to five hours, with three working days to complete it

  • A 90-minute technical interview with the team: you'll walk us through your take-home, then join a working session where you write and tune SQL live

  • A final conversation with our VP of Support Services

  • References, then an offer

The working session is without AI tools, so make sure you're comfortable writing queries from scratch. Download open-source ClickHouse and practise: it's free, easy to install, and great preparation.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

jobs.title: Senior Accounts Receivables Analyst
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We’re looking for a Senior AR Analyst to own billing and collection activities as ClickHouse continues to scale. This role will help ensure the integrity, accuracy, and compliance of our billing, collections, and downstream revenue reporting as we move towards public-company readiness. You’ll work cross-functionally with Revenue Accounting, Sales, Engineering, and other Operations teams to build scalable processes and workflows.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Own end-to-end invoicing and collections activities for pay-as-you-go and prepaid commit customers.

  • Support recurring, and usage-based, billing models across systems for a variety of subscription, invoicing, and payment term configurations.

  • Drive system and process improvements, including AI adoption, automation initiatives, and integrations to streamline workflows.

  • Maintain strong AR health through proactive aging reviews, collections coordination with the sales team, and timely resolution of billing inquiries.

  • Propose quarter-end write-off recommendations and own AR reporting, including aging analysis, allowance for doubtful accounts, and related GL reconciliations.

  • Support monthly accounting close activities, including contract review, usage validation, invoice verification, journal entries, reconciliations, and analytics.

  • Support external audit requirements and manage PBC requests related to billing operations.

  • Support user acceptance testing for new SKU creation, new product launches, pricing models, and business initiatives.

What You Bring Along

  • 3+ years of progressive billing and collections experience at a SaaS or technology company.

  • Experience with marketplace platforms (e.g. AWS, Azure, GCP) and reports.

  • Experience with automation tools and ERP systems (e.g., NetSuite, Stripe, Salesforce CPQ).

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex contracts and data sets.

  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with a focus on accuracy and completeness.

  • Effective communicator with the ability to collaborate cross-functionally and present information clearly.

  • Experience executing internal controls and documentation to support audit and SOX compliance.

jobs.title: Technical Curriculum Developer, Platform - EMEA
jobs.descriptionHtml:
The Learning Team at ClickHouse is growing fast as more and more users discover the power of ClickHouse and its diverse use cases. As part of that growth, we want to ensure our hands-on training experience is best in class.

We are looking for someone to accelerate the way we build technical content and to bring AI-powered tools and agents directly into the learning experience for our students. You will own the infrastructure that powers releases, certification exams, hands-on courses, and learning environments. You will also lead GenAI initiatives to create content more effectively and to build a broader AI-powered user experience.

A typical day as a ClickHouse Technical Curriculum Developer, Platform:

  • Manage the infrastructure that supports our Content as Code

    • New content PRs are thoroughly tested and easy to preview

    • Merged PRs are automatically released

    • Courses are periodically checked to ensure they are working properly

    • Courses are easily updated with new features

  • Lead the Learning team’s adoption of AI and GenAI:

    • build tools, prompts, and workflows to go from topic to course faster

    • Design and build AI-powered agents and tools for students

    • Evaluate new AI/GenAI capabilities and models as they emerge

  • Write and maintain provisioning and grading scripts for hands-on certification exams

  • Debugging issues that affect learners, instructors, and exam candidates

  • Building and running observability for everything learning: usage, failures, catalog health, dashboards, and alerts

  • Building and running analytics for user activity across all learning tools

  • Design and maintain hands-on lab environments across all training formats

Requirements:

  • 5+ years of experience with technical curriculum development on databases and/or distributed systems

  • 3+ years of experience in a technical education infrastructure or DevOps role (e.g. building and operating lab or sandbox environments)

  • Experience with machine learning applications and/or GenAI focused on content generation, developer tooling, and AI agents

  • 3+ years of experience building certification infrastructure including grading scripts for hands-on assessments

  • Strong scripting and automation skills, including experience with infrastructure as code, CI/CD pipelines, and GitHub

  • A self-motivated attitude that provides you with the desire and determination to complete projects in a fast-paced startup environment

  • Ability to learn new technologies quickly and effectively

  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to write clear runbooks and technical documentation

  • You have a high level of responsibility, ownership, and accountability

Bonus points:

  • Experience with SQL

  • Experience with ClickHouse database

  • Experience with one or more Cloud Service Providers such as AWS, GCP, or Azure

  • Ability to work cross-functionally amongst engineering, support, product, and development teams

  • Technical degree (e.g., Computer Science or related field)

You'll love this role if:

  • You thrive working at the intersection of engineering, AI, and education, building systems that directly impact how people learn

  • You are self-driven, curious, and eager to continuously learn and grow

  • You possess a mindset of teamwork, global engagement, empathy, and a drive for solving challenging problems

jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer, Support Operations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Most companies treat support as a cost center. We treat it as an engineering challenge and a product opportunity.

Support Operations Engineering is an engineering function inside ClickHouse’s Support Services organization. We build the systems that decide how customers get help from the moment they describe their problem to the moment it’s resolved. This role will help shape how Support Services, RevOps, GTM, and core Engineering teams collaborate on customers. This is not a tools team. About a third of our work directly supports the support organization. The rest is building experiences and systems that change how ClickHouse works with its customers in more effective, streamlined ways.

What you will be doing

You’ll design and build the systems that sit between ClickHouse’s customers and the teams who serve them. The work is varied by design, and you’ll move between problem types as priorities shift:

  • Intelligent routing and decision systems. Software that decides where work should go and who should handle it, weighing many signals at once, and is built to adapt as the business scales.

  • AI-powered customer experiences. Customer-facing and internal experiences that understand what someone needs, recommend the best next step, and know when to hand off to a human.

  • Internal platforms and tooling. Applications that give Support, RevOps, and GTM teams the leverage to work faster and more accurately, built to production standards.

  • Integrations and data flow. Connections across Salesforce, live chat, incident management, Slack, GitHub, and more, so workflows and data move cleanly between systems.

  • Automation and observability. Systems that remove repetitive work, surface what’s breaking, and give teams confidence in what they’re running.

Across all of it, you’ll partner with core Engineering to ship to production, and own what you build: code review, testing, monitoring, and continuous improvement.

What you bring along:

  • 3–5 years building and shipping full-stack software in production, with tools like TypeScript/JavaScript, Node.js, and React (or comparable)

  • Experience developing with APIs, webhooks, and integrations between distributed systems

jobs.title: Senior Technical Customer Support Engineer - India
jobs.descriptionHtml:
We are currently growing our support team at ClickHouse who provides excellent service to our customers around the world. We are seeking a Senior Technical Support Engineer to join our global Support Engineering team. We hope to find you ready to take on a large variety of tasks related to our customers locally in India as well as more regionally across APJ and EMEA. This is a customer-facing role that will include customer interactions via chat, calls, Slack messages, and virtual meetings over video. You will be owning a wide variety of tasks: from triaging support tickets to user community support, helping with both pre- and post- sales customer activities, partnering with our Go To Market team with deeply technical aspects of POCs, and suggesting improvements to how we do things in Support at ClickHouse. This is a great opportunity for someone ready to roll-up their sleeves and help us expand our regional presence in India!

What you will be doing:

  • Supporting and guiding our ClickHouse users, customers, and prospects via cases, chat, Slack, community, and meetings

  • Develop solutions based on ClickHouse Cloud and ClickHouse open-source that can be shared with our users, community, and customers via documentation, knowledge base, blogs, meetups, webinars, and training

  • Work closely with our global Support Services, Engineering, Go to Market, and Product Management teams to help define functionality required by users and customers

  • Assist with mentoring, training, and sharing your knowledge with colleagues, users, and customers 

And of course:

  • You will deliver excellent customer service as a first-line technical engineer and representative of ClickHouse. Our Support Engineers provide professional response, on-call coverage, and guidance within the required Service Level Agreements ("SLAs") on technical cases that are opened via a ticketing system, email, Slack, chat, and/or phone

  • You will build strong, trusted relationships with colleagues, customers, and partners

What you bring along:

  • Technical breadth and depth in ClickHouse open-source or Cloud, or in domains relevant to ClickHouse, such as: SQL databases, OLAP, cloud-native SaaS, distributed systems, Kubernetes, Docker

  • Previous technical experience in roles such as Support Engineer, Technical Account Manager, Database Administrator, Site Reliability Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Software Engineer, and/or Systems Engineer

  • Be present and available according to the scheduling required to deliver high-quality 24x7 Support in a global, distributed environment

  • Strong written and verbal English communication skills and the ability to work fully remote with reliable connectivity

  • A mindset of teamwork, global engagement, empathy, and solving challenging problems

  • A sense of adventure and urgency in building the most scalable, high-performing, largest, and fastest databases on the planet

  • The ability to build trusted relationships with colleagues, customers, and partners

  • You are self-driven, curious, and eager to continuously learn and grow

Bonus points:

  • Experience with ClickHouse

  • Experience with OSS and open-source technologies, as a user, community member, or contributor

  • Experience with Azure, GCP or AWS

  • Experience with data pipelines such as Kafka, Kinesis, Spark, RabbitMQ, or others

Perks

jobs.title: Senior Design Engineer - Design System & Platform UI
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About the Team
The Design System team owns Click UI - the open-source Design System of ClickHouse. It is the shared UI foundation for ClickHouse Cloud and several other projects. We operate the system as a service and as the clear entry point for all ClickHouse UI work. We focus on building React components that are accessible, performant, well-documented, token-driven, and capable of resolving challenging product requirements.

What You Will Do

  • Research, build, and maintain accessible React components and their APIs on headless accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) primitives. Keyboard interaction, focus management, and theming are part of each component from the start.

  • Work on the library enhancements, focusing on consistent and intuitive components API and developer experience improvements. Enable complex migrations with codemods and semantic versioning.

  • Maintain the shared reliable infrastructure: Storybook, unit, interaction E2E and visual regression tests, accessibility gates, and a reliable release process.

  • Drive adoption: high quality documentation, usage guidelines, migration guides, issue intake and triage (including open-source issues), and code review with product teams.

  • Build the AI-assisted layer: Figma-to-code, component scaffolding, and guardrails that keep AI-generated UI on-token, on-pattern, and accessible.

What We Are Looking For

  • Experience: 6+ years of frontend engineering. You have built or maintained a production design system that multiple teams use, including its migrations and breaking changes.

  • Core Stack: Deep knowledge of React, TypeScript, semantic HTML, and CSS architecture at scale (SASS, CSS Modules, CSS variables, CSS-in-JS). Experience with component API design (atomic design, composition, controlled and uncontrolled, polymorphic patterns) and headless primitives such as React Aria, Ark UI or Radix.

  • Accessibility and Tokens: Working knowledge of WCAG 2.x and WAI-ARIA. You implement and test keyboard navigation, focus management, and screen-reader behavior yourself. Experience with design-token architecture and tools (Style Dictionary, Terrazzo, DTCG, or equivalent) and Figma variables sync.

  • System Mindset: You treat the design system as a product with internal customers. You write clear documentation, review for consistency across the library, and mentor through code review. You measure success by adoption, not by component count. You are fluent in Figma and use AI coding tools (for example Claude Code or Cursor).

  • Ideal Backgrounds: Design system or UI/UX platform teams at developer tools, B2B SaaS, or cloud platforms, or frontend platform roles with a shared UI library and multi-team consumers.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

jobs.title: Senior Consulting Engineer - EMEA
jobs.descriptionHtml:
ClickHouse is the open-source, real-time analytical database behind a lot of today's AI. More than 4,000 companies build on ClickHouse, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Tesla and Meta.

As a Consulting Engineer, you're the hands-on engineer on our customers' most important projects. When a customer needs to migrate, integrate, or prove ClickHouse on a real workload, you work in the build alongside their engineers: you design it, build it, test it and hand it over.

You'll work on a broad mix of projects for customers across EMEA, from moving large workloads off other databases to building new real-time analytics on ClickHouse. Each one is scoped with clear goals from the start, so you know what success looks like and can get stuck in. It's a fast way to build deep experience across lots of different data problems.

The consulting function at ClickHouse is less than a year old, so you'll help shape how ClickHouse delivers this work as the team grows. Between projects you take cases alongside support engineers, which keeps you close to day-to-day support.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Turn customer goals into a scoped project with measurable success criteria, sizing and a timeline

  • Design a target architecture and prove it against the customer's own data: schema and engine design, capacity and sizing, proofs of concept

  • Do the build: implementation, pipelines and integrations, migration execution, tooling and automation

  • Measure it before it matters, with benchmarking, load and functional testing, then support the cutover

  • Tune what production reveals, then hand over with an engagement report and knowledge transfer, so the customer's team can run it without you

  • Take L1 to L3 cases alongside support engineers when you're between projects

  • Feed what you see in the field back to Product and Engineering, and turn your work into reference architectures, knowledge base articles and blog posts

  • Work in a constant feedback loop with the Pre-sales team to ensure that the demos and POCs they present are credible when you put them into production

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • 5+ years delivering hands-on technical work for customers, whether your title was consultant, professional services, solutions architect, senior support, SRE or something else

  • Real depth in databases, whether analytical, transactional or relational

  • Hands-on SQL. You regularly write complex queries from scratch, and tune and debug them yourself

  • You've owned implementations, migrations or POCs for external customers from start to finish

  • Hands-on cloud experience (AWS, GCP and/or Azure)

  • You've deployed and run workloads on Kubernetes yourself

  • You've run distributed systems, such as distributed databases, in production

  • You give precise technical answers and explain them clearly

  • Fluent English

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience with ClickHouse

  • Hands-on Splunk experience

  • Migrating analytical workloads from systems such as PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery or Elastic

  • Terraform

  • Data pipelines and streaming, such as Kafka, Kinesis, Spark or Debezium

  • Python, Bash or Go

  • Involvement in open source, as a user, contributor or community member

GOOD TO KNOW

  • This role is remote within EMEA, in a country where ClickHouse already hires

  • Travel to customer sites is part of the job, up to 35% of your time, depending on the project: some need none, others weekly visits

  • You'll join our EMEA Support Services team, where Support Engineers, Consulting Engineers and TAM Architects work as one team

  • You'll be part of the on-call rotation, about one week a quarter, with time off in lieu if you're paged at a weekend

HOW WE HIRE

  • A 30-minute call with our recruiter

  • A conversation with the hiring manager

  • A take-home exercise, designed to take three to four hours, with three working days to complete it

  • A 90-minute technical interview with the team: you'll walk us through your take-home, then join a working session where you write and tune SQL live

  • A final conversation with our VP of Support Services

  • References, then an offer

The working session is without AI tools, so make sure you're comfortable writing queries from scratch. Download open-source ClickHouse and practise: it's free, easy to install, and great preparation.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

jobs.title: Solution Architect-North Central
jobs.descriptionHtml:
THE ROLE

As an Enterprise Solutions Architect at ClickHouse, you'll own the technical side of the sales cycle for enterprise accounts in the North Central United States. This role serves our Enterprise segment across the North Central region, and the ideal candidate would be based in Minneapolis or Chicago.

You'll engage with data platform engineers, architects, SRE, and the VP who owns the standard - and your job is to design something that satisfies all of them and then prove it at production scale. Getting an enterprise team there usually means moving them off something else, so most of your work is making that migration credible: the architecture, benchmarks run against their own data, and a plan their engineers believe they can execute.

This is a role for engineers who want the hard version of the problem: real scale, real constraints, and an incumbent to displace. Prior pre-sales experience helps but isn't required - technical depth is non-negotiable.

WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING

  • Own the technical evaluation for enterprise accounts - from discovery through POC or competitive bake-off, architecture sign-off, security review, and first production workload.

  • Engage across a wider set of stakeholders than a single team: data platform engineers, architects, SRE, security, and the executive who owns the standard. Design solutions that hold up with all of them in the room.

  • Design for production scale - sizing, sharding and replication strategy, ingestion topology, tiered storage, cost modeling, and what happens when something fails at 3am.

  • Win competitive displacements against Elasticsearch, Splunk, Snowflake, BigQuery, Druid, Pinot, and homegrown systems, using benchmarks the customer's own team can reproduce.

  • Own the migration plan - sequencing, dual-run, validation, and cutover - so the customer's team can see exactly how they get to production.

  • Clear the security and procurement path: questionnaires, compliance artifacts, network and identity architecture, and BYOC or private deployment requirements.

  • Partner closely with Enterprise AEs to progress and close opportunities - you own the technical win, they own the commercial close. Build the TCO case against the incumbent/competition together.

  • Advocate for customer needs internally with Product and Engineering - you're the voice of the technical buyer inside ClickHouse.

  • Contribute reference architectures, benchmark harnesses, migration guides, and objection handling material that help the team scale what's working.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • Deep technical foundation in data infrastructure - built through experience as a data engineer, platform engineer, software engineer, DBA, or solutions architect.

  • Production experience with analytical databases (ClickHouse, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Druid, Pinot, Vertica) and with operating them, not just querying them.

  • Distributed systems judgment: partitioning, replication, consistency trade-offs, query execution, and a felt sense for where things break under load.

  • Fluency across the modern data stack - Kafka and CDC pipelines, orchestration, object storage, BI tools, and at least one major cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure) at architecture level.

  • Experience running a technical evaluation against a named competitor and winning it, including designing the migration off the incumbent and the parts of it that are genuinely hard.

  • Customer-facing experience with real stakes - pre-sales, consulting, technical account management, or a staff-level engineering role that put you in front of customers.

  • Strong written and verbal communication. You can whiteboard with a staff engineer in the morning and present to a VP of Engineering in the afternoon.

  • Comfort with longer cycles and more stakeholders. Enterprise evaluations don't close in three weeks, and you know how to keep one moving without letting it stall.

  • Willingness to say ClickHouse isn't the right tool for a given workload when that's true.

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

Equal Opportunity & Privacy

ClickHouse provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type based on factors such as race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Please see here for our Privacy Statement.

jobs.title: Head of Developer Relations
jobs.descriptionHtml:
ClickHouse started as an open-source project that developers picked up on their own, told each other about, and built companies on. That community is still the reason most people first hear of us, and it is why ClickHouse Cloud fills with new users every day. As the database becomes a platform for real-time analytics, data warehousing, observability, and AI workloads, the community has more to learn from us and more to teach us than ever. Developer relations is how we hold up our end of that relationship.

As Head of Developer Relations, you’ll own how developers discover ClickHouse, get productive on it, and bring others along: the developer experience, the technical content that teaches it, the channels where developers find it, and the community that carries it. You’ll lead our global team of developer advocates and give the function the goals, systems, and investment of a core growth channel. You’ll partner closely with product marketing engineers, field marketing in every region, and product and engineering, and you’ll inherit a strong, globally distributed team and a community that has been generous with us for years. If you believe developer relations starts with helping people, that trust is the only thing that compounds, and that the work should be measured like any other growth investment, this is a rare seat.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Lead, coach, and grow a globally distributed team of developer advocates, and set ClickHouse’s long-term developer and community strategy with marketing, product, and engineering leadership, turned into a multi-year plan with headcount, budget, and investment priorities

  • Own the developer experience from the outside in: track time to first query and getting-started completion, run friction logs on the onboarding path and docs, and own the feedback loop into product and engineering on what developers are building, where they get stuck, and what they want next

  • Own the Developer Relations budget and represent the function to customers, partners, and the open-source community, on stage and on a podcast

  • Set targets across the whole function: community growth and engagement on Slack, Reddit, GitHub, YouTube, and your advocates’ own platforms, developer-experience measures, and content and channel reach, and report on them like any growth channel

  • Build the champions program into a real force, with clear tracks for customers, open-source users, and independent voices, so the community grows the community

  • Build DevRel’s owned channels into audiences: YouTube, newsletter, podcast, and advocates’ own platforms, with a content system that turns one talk or demo into a tutorial, a video, and posts, and creator partnerships that extend reach beyond our own

  • Run the developer-event portfolio as one input to that engine: meetups, conference talks, and practitioner-led sessions chosen with intent, each producing recorded and written material, with attendance that becomes a signal the business can use

  • Shape developer education and technical content, from tutorials and workshops to courses and certification, in tandem with the training team, product marketing engineers, and the organic and AEO team on a shared publishing map (which channels matter most, what belongs on each, and who owns it), so each piece goes where developers learn now: docs, video, and AI assistants

  • Work with regional field marketing to support in-region developer programs and the startup and partner ecosystem

What You Bring

  • Experience leading a developer relations or community team at an infrastructure company, with direct management of 4 or more people and strong leadership of a distributed team

  • Deep technical skill: you can write the demo, ship the tutorial, and go deep with engineers on how a database works

  • Experience running developer events and speaking programs where the room was chosen with intent

  • Experience building developer education or content programs that scaled beyond the people who made them: tutorials, courses, video, or docs that developers still find and use

  • Experience growing owned developer channels (YouTube, newsletter, podcast, or similar) to a real audience, and a point of view on how developers find technical content now, including through AI assistants

  • Experience building or scaling developer programs, including a champions, ambassador, or MVP program, with a track record of innovation

  • Experience putting numbers on community work and defending them, from growth and engagement to the connection with signups and pipeline, without turning advocates into salespeople

  • Comfort operating globally and cross-functionally with product, engineering, product marketing, and field teams

  • Willingness to travel at least 25% of the time

  • DevRel or community leadership around an open-source project with a real community, and experience growing that community without losing its trust

Perks

  • Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

  • Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

  • Equity in the company - Every new team member who joins our company receives stock options.

  • Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

  • A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

  • Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

Equal Opportunity & Privacy
